# Third-party source

Upstream material that is not available as a package is kept here, unmodified,
under its own licence. Everything else libtuya builds on is an ordinary
dependency (see `NOTICE.md`).

## home-assistant-core

A snapshot of the Tuya integration from
[home-assistant/core](https://github.com/home-assistant/core), Apache-2.0
(`home-assistant-core/LICENSE.md`). `home-assistant-core/UPSTREAM` records the
release and commit it was taken from.

| Path | Used for |
|---|---|
| `homeassistant/components/tuya/` | Source of `libtuya/data/ha_tuya.json`, generated by `scripts/gen_ha_tables.py`. Nothing here is imported at run time. |
| `tests/components/tuya/fixtures/` | Dumps of real devices, used as test input. |
| `tests/components/tuya/snapshots/` | The entities Home Assistant creates for those devices, used to check that libtuya creates the same ones. |

Rules:

- Do not edit these files. Fix things upstream, or in libtuya's own code.
- To update, run `scripts/sync-upstream.sh <home-assistant release tag>`. It
  replaces the snapshot, rewrites `UPSTREAM` and regenerates the data file.
  Then set the `tuya-device-handlers` and `tuya-device-sharing-sdk` pins in
  `pyproject.toml` to the versions in the snapshot's `manifest.json` (a test
  checks they agree) and run the tests.
- None of this is shipped in the wheel except the generated data file and the
  licence text.
